column2: The Weave has led an old spellsinger into your glade. The traveller remembers little of the road that brought them here, but they are ready to put themselves at your service.
It is a sign. They are welcome.
It might be cursed.

All the children of Isha are bound to the Weave, but you have always felt the forest more keenly than the others. The trees seem to whisper when you pass. Perhaps your guardian could teach you to listen, and to sing back.
I will be a wise spellsinger!
For some time now your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has been pestering you, begging you to teach [From.GetHerHim] how to touch the Weave and cast spells.
You may have some potential...
Go away. This is not a game.
Your guardian has agreed to take you as an apprentice and teach you the ways of the Weave.
I will soon be a powerful spellsinger!
Your [GetFromRelation] refused to teach you magic, claiming you lack what it takes to handle such a dangerous power.
I could! How can you say that?
There is much a spellsinger must know before the Weave can be trusted to them. What should [From.GetFirstName] learn next?
A spellsinger must tell light from darkness.
A spellsinger must always strive for perfection.
A spellsinger must never lose their calm.
Enough. Let us turn to the Weave itself.
For weeks you and your [GetFromRelation] have talked of how a spellsinger must keep a clear mind and judge the world without favour, lest they be deceived by the lies of Chaos or of lesser races.
Of course. We are the enlightened kin.
For weeks you and your [GetFromRelation] have talked of how a spellsinger must always work at their best: studying new songs, perfecting every ritual, leaving nothing to chance.
I would not want to blow anything up. By mistake.
For weeks you and your [GetFromRelation] have talked of how a spellsinger must stay calm, lest passion cloud the senses and twist the spell against its caster.
But is it not passion that gives purpose to the Hunt?

All in Athel Loren is balance: summer and winter, death and rebirth, light and darkness. The great cycles of the seasons rule the lives of all beings, and the Asrai do not shun any part of the Weave. Highweavers heal and preserve, while Darkweavers hunt, twist and terrify the forest's enemies. Which path calls to you?
I will follow the path of light.
I will follow the dark path.
It has become clear that your student [From.GetFirstName] has chosen the path of the Highweaver, to heal the sickness and corruption that would tarnish the forest and keep it pure.
It has become clear that your student [From.GetFirstName] has chosen the path of the Darkweaver, to twist and terrify those who would harm Athel Loren.
I am proud of [From.GetHerHim].
That is... still acceptable, I suppose.
You have taught your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] much of what you know over the years. Is [From.GetSheHe] ready to be named a spellsinger?
The time has come.
No. [From.GetSheHeCap] never will be.
After many years of study, your [GetFromRelation] has named you a spellsinger, an apprentice no longer. The Weave answers when you sing to it now.
And yet there is so much still to learn...
Your [GetFromRelation] has judged you unfit to be a spellsinger and sent you away. Your years of study are over.
Years wasted!

Spellsingers are the mages of the Asrai. Through their bond with the Weave of Athel Loren they can reshape the forest around them. After your long studies, your liege has given you a place at court among them.
The forest speaks to me.
You have spent decades poring over ancient lore, meditating deep in the forest and seeking visions from the spirits, all for nothing. Your gift for magic is mediocre at best.
There is no point going on...
You have dwelt in darkness so long that its taint has begun to cloud your senses, filling you with senseless hatred and foul thoughts. The balance must be restored.
Light to balance the darkness.
I shall endure it.

Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] is plagued by [From.GetHerHis] dealings with the dark powers. As a Highweaver it is your duty to restore the balance of [From.GetHerHis] soul so that [From.GetSheHe] can go on serving the forest.
I will prepare the ritual.
The ritual of [From.GetTitledFirstName] has calmed your troubled soul. The dark powers are bound to your will once more, to be unleashed only on the enemies of Athel Loren.
And soon they will be.
For all [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s efforts, you are still plagued by bloody visions and twisted dreams. The dark powers you have called on to flay your enemies are devouring your soul.
I *will* contain them!
